evidence_checked: jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_8384.txt (sha256 ef8f894b... re-hashed; quote 22147-22631 matches; sections 15 and 21 read)
reasoning: Identity, page location (4 FR 3722, FR issue of August 26, 1939) and the one-row inventory are correct: EO 8226 restates section 15 of EO 7845 and is effective as of June 30, 1939. The ending source is correct and the date March 2, 1940 is the stated effective date of EO 8384 section 21, with the signing date disclosed as the alternative. The claim nonetheless records the mechanism as 'amend' while EO 8384 says it 'shall supersede' EO 8226 and the claim's own reason calls the end an express supersession; a wrong mechanism is a ground for rejection under the review rules. The earlier-end search is also described as finding the number in the form 'Executive Order No. 8226', which the held corpus does not contain. No earlier end was found in my own search. Correcting the mechanism to supersede and the search description would likely make the claim acceptable.

defects.source_says: EO 9607 is signed August 30, 1945 (10 FR 11191, issue of August 31, 1945; OFR catalog signing_date 1945-08-30), and every judgment_reason in the claim states 'the signing date August 30, 1945 is the end date'. 1942-08-30 also precedes EO 9301's own signing on February 9, 1943, so the recorded end is impossible and contradicts the claim's own reasons.

evidence_checked: cruden.py number EO:9301 (EO 9607 FR and APP texts only)
reasoning: Identity, the five-row inventory, the duration-of-the-war own-terms analysis and the savings reasoning are sound, and EO 9607 does revoke EO 9301 by number with no delayed effective date. But all five first_end dates and the whole_order_end date are 1942-08-30, three years before the revocation and before EO 9301 itself was signed. The claim's text gives August 30, 1945 throughout, so the date fields are wrong and internally inconsistent. Reject; with the date corrected to 1945-08-30 the remainder of the analysis would stand.

defects.claim_says: No earlier end is held. The order states no period, date or condition. ... No held order revokes, supersedes or rewrites this order before EO 9830. unresolved_material_gaps: []
defects.source_says: The amended paragraph lists 'One general counsel' under Subdivision XL of Schedule A, the Board of Investigation and Research (FR contents on 7 FR 363; EO 9004 Schedule A 'XL. BOARD OF INVESTIGATION AND RESEARCH (Transportation Act of 1940)'). The held Transportation Act of 1940, 54 Stat. 898 (jobs/source-ladder text, sha256 f2592428...), section 306 provides: 'This part shall cease to have effect at the end of two years after its enactment unless extended by a proclamation of the President for an additional period which shall not exceed two years.' The Act was approved September 18, 1940, so the Board's statutory life ended no later than September 18, 1944 absent a further Act. That is a held, dated candidate for an earlier end (the position and its exception losing their object) that the claim neither cites nor resolves; the dossier's own prior review flagged it as material.

evidence_checked: jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9027.txt (sha256 f76b49e1... re-hashed; spans match; order read in full)
jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9830.txt (re-hashed; enacting clause 'effective May 1, 1947:', Part III list row 'No. 9027 of January 16, 1942.')
dossier evidence ACT:EO:9027>EO:9830 review and producer_d6 notes
cruden.py number EO:9027 (0 matches; EO 9830 lists it as 'No. 9027')
reasoning: Identity, inventory and the EO 9830 revocation (effective May 1, 1947) are correctly quoted. The earlier-end test is not adequate. EO 9027 excepts one general counsel position of the Board of Investigation and Research, a temporary statutory body. The repository holds the creating statute, whose section 306 ends the Board two years after enactment unless extended by proclamation for at most two more years, so the Board ceased no later than September 18, 1944 unless Congress extended it. Under the owner's evidence ruling, a sunset of the body whose position the order excepts is a stated reason the command may have lost its object before 1947. Whether that is an end and on what date (1942 or 1944, depending on any proclamation) must be investigated or recorded as a gap. The claim instead says no earlier end is held and lists no material gap. Reject until the Board's termination and any extension proclamation are traced, or the gap is recorded.
